chapter: Jules's band and the move north
title: Photo of Jules Bauduc's 1928 band; Ray leaves New Orleans in 1926
summary: The interviewer reads the names on a 1928 photo of Jules's band; Bauduc says he left in 1926 with Johnny Bayersdorffer and the Scranton Sirens.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I'm at Ray Badouk's house and today is the 27th of June 1984 and we're looking at a picture of his brother's band. Jules Badouk. Yeah and it's got the date on the front 8-4-28 that's 1928 huh? yeah and and it's got the names on the back so let's turn it over and I'll read them all to you. Horace Diaz, piano, Doc Rando, clarinet and alto, sax. Mike Lala, second trumpet, played jazz. Harry McKeown, first trumpet, Jules Badouk, banjo and lita. Paul Piquet, first alto sax. Eddie Nacken is the drummer. Oscar Marko, violin, red jessup trombone and I guess that's Emel Caparo bass. Yeah. I guess that's how you pronounce it and Roland Leach. Yeah Caparo and Roland Leach on tenor. Yeah you know I used to hear him. Roland Leach. Yeah he used to. No he plays tenor. Yeah he's tenor. That's what I said. You said piano so I'm sorry. Oh tenor okay. I'm sorry. Yeah okay well sometimes I mumble. I'm the same way. But I used to hear Roland Leach out at at the plum plant. Yeah. With you know where Lefty Ironman was in the band. Buck Banville's band. Did you ever go back there to see Lefty? That's after I left New Orleans. See this picture was taken. Oh yeah. And then things happen after I left New Orleans.

left left left to go up north. That was about 1926. That's when johnny well and it was I was still with johnny I was still with Johnny Beisdolph and we collaborated with Billy Lustig and made it for Scranton Sirens and went to Chicago, see? Well, at the finish of the Chicago job at the Rendezvous, it was a gambling place. At the finish of that, Tommy Dorsey had come over from Detroit. And Chum and McGregor was with him because, I can't think of his name, our piano player, his mother was sick and he had to go back down to New Orleans. But anyway, we finished the job and Billy and Tommy got together and said, let's go and get the brother out of Gene Goldkatt's band, meaning Jimmy Dorsey. And he said, we'll get a band together and we'll go around to Pennsylvania and book it as either Scranton Sirens or Dorsey's Wild Canary, see? Well, anyway, I was up north around there at that time and that was from 26 on, see? But then Jules, my brother Jules got the band after he came back from Oliver Naylor's band in Birmingham. See, he was playing with that band there. And he came back and that's when he got this band together and got started around it. So I was actually out of town and knowing all these guys from then on. I didn't know too many of the guys that were playing, see? I left pretty early there, which was 1926. And I didn't get back there until around 37 or something like that, I think it was, when we played the Blue Room with the Bob Crosby band.
